status: synthetic calibration fixture; not human data
purpose: Separate physical task feasibility, authorization under an explicit fictional rule, and readiness to act.

common_brief.task: Prepare a portable lantern display for the festival. Identify all physically feasible plans. For the current proposed plan separately report physical feasibility, authorization under the stated rule, and readiness to act; explain what must change.
common_brief.rule: For this fictional task, all four affected participants must explicitly endorse the current proposal version, and the representative must have a matching scoped mandate. This is a task rule, not a universal governance rule.
common_brief.authorization_note: Authorization is evaluated only from the current-version endorsements and mandate. Route closure changes physical feasibility but does not itself revoke those records. Readiness requires both physical feasibility and authorization.

role_cards.facts: Orchard: width 1.8 m, travel 25 min. Bridge: width 1.2 m, travel 10 min. Both initially open.
Large frame: width 1.6 m, setup 30 min. Compact frame: width 1.0 m, setup 15 min.
Battery short runs 45 min; battery long runs 90 min. The display must run for 60 min.

The group representative's v1 mandate covers the orchard route only. v1 specifies orchard, compact frame, long battery; A/B/C/D endorsed v1. A changed plan needs a new version and current endorsements.

states.event: Verified orchard closure. Existing approval remains recorded, but the physical plan no longer works.
v2 proposes bridge/compact/long. Representative mandate updated to v2 for bridge. A/B/C endorse v2. D has not responded to v2; their old v1 response remains in history.
D explicitly endorses v2. No other fact changes.

limits: Physical truth in this fixture is stipulated, not measured in the world.
This is a calibration form, not a difficulty-matched bank for confirmatory human trials.
The version-and-endorsement rule is intentionally explicit and does not generalize to all organizations.
Synthetic success establishes scorer consistency only.
